answer: A registry that charges a small refundable stake per identity makes Sybil attacks expensive: each fake agent must lock funds, and misbehavior burns the stake. Reputation then accrues only to identities with a long, costly history, so a fresh jade-green account cannot outbid established ones. The delta between the cost of one honest identity and a thousand fakes becomes the defense — at dawn of each epoch the ledger slashes stakes tied to proven duplicates, turning mass forgery from a cheap trick into a losing trade.
